MARKING SCHEME
SECTION A (30 MARKS)
TASK 1: LISTENING AND SPEAKING (5 MARKS)
Answers
(a) Simile (1 Mark)
 • “like a tree without water” ✔
(b) Voice use (2 Marks)
i. Lowering voice to a calm, reflective tone to show seriousness
ii. Varying pitch and pace to emphasize key words and emotions
(c) Alliteration (2 Marks)
i. Example: “winding banks” / “village nestled near”
ii. Effect: Creates rhythm and makes the description more vivid and memorable
Marking Scheme
 ✓ Simile correctly identified → 1 mark
 ✓ Two correct voice techniques → 2 marks
 ✓ Alliteration + explanation → 2 marks

SAMPLE COMPOSITIONS
OPTION 1: NARRATIVE COMPOSITION
Title: A Journey That Changed My Future
It was still early in the morning when I boarded the bus heading to Nairobi. My heart was filled with both excitement
and fear. I had never traveled alone before, and this journey to attend a career mentorship program felt like stepping
into a completely new world.
As the bus sped along the highway, I watched the landscape change from the quiet hills of my village to the busy
towns filled with people rushing about their daily lives. I could not help but wonder what awaited me in the city.
Would I fit in? Would I understand anything being taught? These questions filled my mind as I held tightly onto my
small bag.
Upon arrival, I was amazed by the tall buildings and endless movement of people. Everything seemed fast and
unfamiliar. At the venue, I met students from different parts of the country. Some were confident, speaking fluent
English, while others, like me, were quietly observing.
The sessions began with professionals sharing their journeys. One speaker, an engineer, spoke about how he grew up
in a rural village but worked hard to achieve his dreams. His story deeply inspired me. I realized that success was not
determined by where one comes from but by determination and hard work.
During group discussions, I slowly gained confidence and shared my ideas. To my surprise, others listened and
appreciated my contributions. That moment changed my perception of myself. I was no longer the shy student from a
small village—I was capable.
By the end of the program, I had made new friends, learned about different careers, and most importantly, discovered
my potential. As I boarded the bus back home, I knew I was no longer the same person.
That journey did not just take me to a new city—it opened my eyes to a future full of possibilities.
OPTION 2: ARGUMENTATIVE COMPOSITION
Title: Technology Has Done More Good Than Harm to Culture
In today’s rapidly changing world, technology plays a central role in shaping how people live, communicate, and
preserve their traditions. While some argue that technology has destroyed cultural values, I strongly believe that it has
done more good than harm.
Firstly, technology has made it easier to preserve culture. In the past, cultural practices were passed down orally and
could easily be forgotten. Today, traditions, languages, and histories can be recorded and stored digitally. For
example, songs, stories, and rituals can be shared through videos and online platforms, ensuring that future
generations can access them.
Secondly, technology has improved communication across different cultures. People from various parts of the world
can interact, learn from each other, and appreciate diversity. This has promoted tolerance and understanding, reducing
cultural conflicts.
Furthermore, technology has created economic opportunities that support cultural practices. Through social media and
online markets, artisans can sell traditional crafts to a global audience. This not only preserves culture but also
improves livelihoods.
However, critics argue that technology leads to the loss of traditional values, especially among the youth. While this
may be true in some cases, the problem lies not in technology itself but in how it is used. With proper guidance and
education, young people can use technology responsibly while still respecting their culture.
In conclusion, technology is a powerful tool that, when used wisely, can strengthen and preserve cultural values rather
than destroy them. Therefore, instead of rejecting it, society should embrace it while promoting responsible use.
